content.text:
Porto Notes is built and shipping in `dist/`. ## What's there **`src/richtext.ts`** — the core of the feature. Users type inline tags in a textarea, so the body is untrusted markup. It's tokenised and rendered into DOM nodes the app constructs itself (`createElement` / `createTextNode`); `innerHTML` is never used. Only `
` are produced — anything else shows as the literal text the user typed. Entities are decoded *before* URL scheme checks (so `javascript:` doesn't slip through), and hrefs are limited to http/https/mailto. Unbalanced tags can't restructure the page: an open-tag stack auto-closes at the end and stray closes are dropped. **`src/storage.ts`** — localStorage under `porto-notes`, seeded from `fixtures.json` on first load and persisted immediately. Everything read back is re-validated field by field, so tampered or stale storage degrades to the seed rather than crashing. **`src/main.ts`** — feed, search, selection and fragment sync. Fragment writes use `replaceState` so typing doesn't fill the history stack. **`index.html`** — the full static shell (form, search, feed exist before JS runs), plus a strict CSP meta. Since nothing needs inline script or style, `script-src 'self'` locks in the no-innerHTML property: a slip in the rendering path can't become script execution. Build is clean under it. ## Element contract `#note-form` / `#title` / `#body` / `#avatar` / submit, `#search`, `#results-line`, `#feed`, `article.note[data-note-id]` with `.note-title` / `.note-body` / `img.note-avatar`. `.note-title` is a real `
